passages.quote: Apparent power (S) is the power delivered to an electrical circuit.
True power (P) is the power consumed by the resistive loads in an electrical circuit.
Unlike true power, reactive power is not useful power because it is stored in the circuit itself.
The total power delivered by the source is the apparent power.
Power factor (pf) is the ratio between true power and apparent power.
It can vary from 1, when the phase angle is 0°, to 0, when the phase angle is 90°.
inductive circuit (L) where current (I) lags voltage (E).
Total Power supplied to an electrical circuit.  It is a combination of the true and reactive power, measured in Volt Amps (VA).

passages.quote: Does not perform any useful work but is essential for maintaining magnetic and electric fields through inductors and capacitors.
passages.cite: Word: AC Generator Theory and Operation.docx, slide 1.23 Power Factor Recall

passages.quote: A three-phase (3φ) system is a combination of three single-phase systems.
produces three separate and equal voltages, each of which is 120° out of phase with the other voltages
Three-phase equipment is smaller in size, weighs less, and is more efficient than single-phase equipment.
They have a wide range of voltages and can be used for single-phase loads.
If the three common ends of each phase are connected at a common point and the other three ends are connected to a 3φ line, it is called a wye, or Y-, connection
If the three phases are connected in series to form a closed loop, it is called a delta, or ∆-, connection.
In a balanced delta load, the line voltage (VL) is equal to the phase voltage (Vφ )
line current (IL) is equal to the phase current (Iφ ).
the total power formulas for delta- and wye-connected loads are identical.
Unbalanced three-phase circuits are indicated by abnormally high currents in one or more of the phases.
the neutral connection in a wye-connected load will carry more current than the phase under a balanced load.

body.text: In AC circuits, current and voltage are normally out of phase, so not all the power produced by the generator can be used to accomplish work.

body.alt: Right triangle with true power P on the base, reactive power Q on the vertical side, apparent power S on the hypotenuse, and angle theta between P and S.

body.text: Apparent power is measured in volt-amperes (VA).
S = I²Z = ITE
True power is measured in watts.
P = I²R = EI cos θ
Reactive power (Q) is expressed in volt-amperes-reactive (VAR). It comes from the expansion and collapse of magnetic and electrostatic fields.
Q = I²X = EI sin θ
Part of the apparent power, called true power, is dissipated by the circuit resistance as heat. The rest is returned to the source by the circuit inductance and capacitance.

checks.q: On the power triangle, which side represents apparent power?
checks.x: Figure 1 shows apparent power S as the hypotenuse, between true power P and reactive power Q. The total power delivered by the source is the apparent power.

checks.q: Why is reactive power not useful power?
o: It is stored in the circuit itself
It exists only in DC circuits
It is consumed by resistive loads
checks.x: Unlike true power, reactive power is not useful power because it is stored in the circuit itself.

In an inductive circuit, the current lags the voltage and is said to have a lagging power factor.

body.alt: Phasor diagram with E on the reference line and current I lagging it by the angle theta.

body.text: In a capacitive circuit, the current leads the voltage and is said to have a leading power factor.

In a balanced wye load, the line voltage is the square root of three times the phase voltage, and:

checks.q: Which is a reason three-phase power systems are used?
o: The equipment is smaller, weighs less, and is more efficient
checks.x: Three-phase equipment is smaller in size, weighs less, and is more efficient than single-phase equipment.

checks.q: A balanced three-phase system has VL = 100 volts, IL = 10 amps, and a power factor of 0.8. Using √3 = 1.73, what is the real power?
A balanced three-phase system has VL = 100 volts and IL = 10 amps. Using √3 = 1.73, what is the apparent power?

In a balanced delta load, how does line voltage compare with phase voltage?
o: Line voltage is √3 times phase voltage
Line voltage is half of phase voltage
checks.x: In a balanced delta load, the line voltage is equal to the phase voltage.

checks.q: In a balanced wye load, how does line current compare with phase current?
o: Line current is √3 times phase current
Line current is three times phase current
checks.x: In a balanced wye load, line current is equal to the phase current.

body.text: In a balanced system, the phasor sum of the three line or phase voltages is zero, and the phasor sum of the three line or phase currents is zero.
When the three load impedances are not equal, the phasor sums and the neutral current are not zero, and the load is unbalanced. This occurs when an open or short circuit appears at the load.

body.alt: A wye load shown balanced, with an open circuit in phase A, and with a short circuit in phase A.

body.text: This may cause damage to equipment if the imbalance is allowed to continue.

checks.q: In a fault condition, what can the neutral connection of a wye-connected load carry?
o: More current than the phase carries under a balanced load
checks.x: In a fault condition, the neutral connection in a wye-connected load will carry more current than the phase under a balanced load.

examples.title: Power in a series R-C circuit
examples.problem: An 80 Ω XC and a 60 Ω resistance are in series with a 120 V source, and the current is 1.2 amps. Find the power factor, true power, reactive power, and apparent power.
steps: pf = cos θ, where θ = arctan(-80/60) = -53°, so pf = 0.60.
examples.answer: pf 0.60, P 86.4 watts, Q 114.9 VAR, S 144 VA

examples.title: Power in a series R-C-L circuit
examples.problem: A series R-C-L circuit has 71.6 V applied, a 4 amp current, and a phase angle of 63.4°. Find the power factor, true power, and apparent power.

facts.q: In what units are apparent, true, and reactive power measured?
facts.a: Apparent power in volt-amperes (VA), true power in watts, and reactive power in volt-amperes-reactive (VAR).

facts.q: Over what range can power factor vary?
facts.a: From 1, when the phase angle is 0°, to 0, when the phase angle is 90°.

facts.q: What does ELI the ICE man help you remember?
facts.a: ELI: in an inductive circuit, current lags voltage. ICE: in a capacitive circuit, current leads voltage.

facts.q: How far apart are the three voltages of a three-phase generator?
facts.a: Each is 120° out of phase with the other voltages.
The three phases are connected in series to form a closed loop.
The three common ends of each phase are connected at a common point, and the other three ends are connected to a 3φ line.

summary.text: Apparent power is S = I²Z = ITE, true power is P = I²R = EI cos θ, and reactive power is Q = I²X = EI sin θ.
ELI the ICE man describes the reactive characteristics of an AC circuit.
Three-phase systems are used because the equipment is smaller, weighs less, and is more efficient.
Unbalanced three-phase circuits are indicated by abnormally high currents in one or more of the phases.
